From b8f8dbf6495850b0babc551377bde754b7bc0eea Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2020 16:25:36 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] drm/vram-helper: Fix use of top-down placement
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Commit 7053e0eab473 ("drm/vram-helper: stop using TTM placement flags")
cleared the BO placement flags if top-down placement had been selected.
Hence, BOs that were supposed to go into VRAM are now placed in a default
location in system memory.

Trying to scanout the incorrectly pinned BO results in displayed garbage
and an error message.

[  146.108127] 
diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/drm_gem_vram_helper.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/drm_gem_vram_helper.c
index 50cad0e4a92e..375c79e23ca5 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/drm_gem_vram_helper.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/drm_gem_vram_helper.c
@@ -140,7 +140,7 @@ static void drm_gem_vram_placement(struct drm_gem_vram_object *gbo,
 	unsigned int c = 0;
 
 	if (pl_flag & DRM_GEM_VRAM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN)
-		pl_flag = TTM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN;
+		invariant_flags = TTM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN;
 
 	gbo->placement.placement = gbo->placements;
 	gbo->placement.busy_placement = gbo->placements;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/drm_gem_vram_helper.c`**
   - The line:
     ```c
     pl_flag = TTM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN;
     ```
     was changed to:
     ```c
     invariant_flags = TTM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN;
     ```
   - This modification adjusts how the top-down placement flag is applied, switching from directly assigning it to the `pl_flag` variable to assigning it to `invariant_flags`.

### Relationships
The modification in the `drm_gem_vram_helper.c` file addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (7053e0eab473) that cleared buffer object (BO) placement flags when top-down placement was selected. The change ensures that the top-down placement flag is correctly utilized, preventing BOs that should be placed in VRAM from being incorrectly allocated in system memory. This fix rectifies issues related to displaying garbage when trying to scanout incorrectly pinned BOs.

drm/vram-helper: Fix use of top-down placement
MIME-Version: 1.0

Commit 7053e0eab473 ("drm/vram-helper: stop using TTM placement flags")
cleared the BO placement flags if top-down placement had been selected.
Hence, BOs that were supposed to go into VRAM are now placed in a default
location in system memory.

Trying to scanout the incorrectly pinned BO results in displayed garbage
and an error message.

Fix the bug by keeping the placement flags. The top-down placement flag
is stored in a separate variable.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de>
Reviewed-by: Christian König <christian.koenig@amd.com>
Fixes: 7053e0eab473 ("drm/vram-helper: stop using TTM placement flags")
Cc: Christian König <christian.koenig@amd.com>

Cc: Daniel Vetter <daniel@ffwll.ch>
Cc: dri-devel@lists.freedesktop.org
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20200921142536.4392-1-tzimmermann@suse.de

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the clearing of buffer object (BO) placement flags when top-down placement was selected, which led to BOs intended for VRAM being placed in a default location in system memory instead. This incorrect placement resulted in display issues and error messages when attempting to scanout the improperly pinned BOs.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void drm_gem_vram_placement(struct drm_gem_vram_object *gbo,
 				   unsigned long pl_flag)
 {
 	u32 invariant_flags = 0;
 	unsigned int i;
 	unsigned int c = 0;
 
 	if (pl_flag & DRM_GEM_VRAM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN)
-		pl_flag = TTM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN;
+		invariant_flags = TTM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN;
 
 	gbo->placement.placement = gbo->placements;
 	gbo->placement.busy_placement = gbo->placements;
 
 	if (pl_flag & DRM_GEM_VRAM_PL_FLAG_VRAM) {
 		gbo->placements[c].mem_type = TTM_PL_VRAM;
 		gbo->placements[c++].flags = TTM_PL_FLAG_WC |
 					     TTM_PL_FLAG_UNCACHED |
 					     invariant_flags;
 	}
 
 	if (pl_flag & DRM_GEM_VRAM_PL_FLAG_SYSTEM || !c) {
 		gbo->placements[c].mem_type = TTM_PL_SYSTEM;
 		gbo->placements[c++].flags = TTM_PL_MASK_CACHING |
 					     invariant_flags;
 	}
 
 	gbo->placement.num_placement = c;
 	gbo->placement.num_busy_placement = c;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < c; ++i) {
 		gbo->placements[i].fpfn = 0;
 		gbo->placements[i].lpfn = 0;
 	}
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (pl_flag & DRM_GEM_VRAM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN)
    pl_flag = TTM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN;
```
Reason:
This code clears the buffer object (BO) placement flags when the top-down placement is selected, which causes the BOs that should be placed in VRAM to instead be placed in a default location in system memory. This incorrect placement leads to display issues and error messages when trying to use these improperly pinned BOs.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (pl_flag & DRM_GEM_VRAM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN)
    invariant_flags = TTM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN;
```
Reason:
This change preserves the top-down placement flag in a separate variable (`invariant_flags`) instead of overwriting the `pl_flag`. This ensures that the correct placement flags are maintained, allowing BOs intended for VRAM to be placed correctly, thus resolving the display issues and errors.
